description:
Execution boundary: planning approved; this issue does not authorize commits, pushes, merges, upstream publication, GitHub comments, live WhatsApp access, or real messages. Revalidate current source/Git state before implementation. Preserve unrelated work, including the already-edited docs/architecture.md. Track this work in the ZAQ Beadwork store even when files belong to the sibling package; do not initialize another store.
Read AGENTS.md in the affected repository. For ZAQ read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md plus the domain policies listed below. Read module documentation before editing. Source navigation uses Serena with bounded fallback if unavailable. Record test results honestly; plan approval is not completed-feature UX approval. Follow repository validation owners; no assertion weakening or unrelated refactors. Existing test changes outside the specifically approved contracts need human approval.

Required domain policies: ../jido_chat_whatsapp/AGENTS.md; README.md host-provided storage; docs/adapter_contracts.md; ZAQ docs/services/system-config.md when reviewing host storage boundaries. No edits to ../jido_chat or Amarula.

Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add:
Repository: ../jido_chat_whatsapp. Owners: lib/jido_chat_whatsapp/transport.ex and transport/amarula_client.ex; use transport/guarded_storage.ex only where needed to preserve existing semantics. Add an optional transport cleanup operation taking trusted connection configuration and opts; suggested concrete signature cleanup(config, opts) -> :ok | {:error, atom}. Old custom transports may omit it and must return unsupported at the calling boundary, never silently succeed.
Resolve exactly the profile/storage selection used by connection startup: explicit storage (including prebuilt Amarula.Storage.Scope) precedes storage_root; explicit storage_root follows existing File behavior; otherwise preserve Amarula's configurable default adapter and AMARULA_DATA_DIR/default root. Factor only the package's existing selection logic so connect and cleanup cannot drift. Reuse Amarula construction/resolution APIs rather than copying upstream defaults; inspect allocation side effects and ensure no transport connection or extra lasting resources are started merely to clear storage. Do not pre-read credentials or require valid identity to clear corrupt saved data.
Delegate profile clearing to Amarula.Storage.clear(scope, profile). File storage clears only that profile; custom storage receives its own state; Split retains host authorization and clears durable + volatile records. No File.rm_rf logic in the adapter/ZAQ, no Split hardcoding, no fallback to File on custom failures. Preserve prebuilt scope state. No managed Mnesia startup or dependency for File/custom stores that do not use it. Scope configuration is trusted host input, not browser input.
Do not change ../jido_chat or Amarula sources/dependency contracts, existing listener logout semantics, or ordinary stop's credential retention. Network/server unlink is not guaranteed without a live connection. Report partial backend cleanup as failure; no false rollback claim. This primitive does not own host runtime supervision or promise cross-store atomicity.

Tests to add before implementation:
Add non-live tests under test/jido/chat/whatsapp/storage_lifecycle_test.exs (or a focused transport cleanup test): default File root in isolated environment, explicit storage_root, explicit File spec, custom backend overriding storage_root, configured default backend, prebuilt scope preserves initialized state, Split DB-callback/RAM routing, selected-profile-only clear, missing profile data/idempotence, callback unsupported/error/throw/exit, corrupt credentials clearable without read. Verify no connect/network call; File works with managed Mnesia absent. Use isolated BEAM for environment/default-backend/Mnesia tests. Keep existing normal stop and running logout regression coverage. Prove partial Split failure and retry without claiming atomic rollback.

Branches/paths validated:
All storage selectors, no listener, absent data, corruption, unsupported capability, partial failure/retry, scope isolation, ordinary stop preservation.

Mocking plan:
Real File backend with per-test temporary directory, real scopes and Split/Mnesia in isolated VM, existing host storage callback fixture for external host boundary. Transport network stub only; do not mock Amarula.Storage.clear or replace internal ownership tests with fake success.

Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content:
Update transport callback docs, docs/adapter_contracts.md cleanup/storage compatibility section, and README storage/lifecycle guidance. Do not edit generated CHANGELOG.md.

Action reuse assessment:
Decision: extend optional package Transport contract and reuse Amarula.Storage.scope/clear plus existing storage selection. Storage.Split.clear already implements host durable + Mnesia clear, but choosing it for every caller would break File/custom upstream users. Existing Transport.logout(conn, opts) needs a live connection; stop(conn, opts) intentionally preserves credentials, so neither substitutes for offline cleanup. Local adapter infrastructure capability, not a ZAQ/Jido Action or tool/workflow. Runtime configuration and effects stay in the transport; returned errors are sanitized atoms. Tests prove backend dispatch and compatibility.

comments.text: Implemented optional Transport.cleanup/2 with shared startup storage selection and upstream Amarula.new resolution. Prebuilt inert cache scopes prevent unrelated cache initialization; no credential reads or connection creation. File/default/configured default/custom/prebuilt/Split cases covered; real Split generation loss after durable clear proves honest partial failure and retry. No managed Mnesia required for File. 29 tests + 1 isolation/idempotence property pass with existing storage lifecycle regressions; package mix quality passes (Dialyzer 0 errors, Doctor 0 failed modules). No jido_chat/Amarula sources changed. Diff remains local.
